design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 0 (move_out_deposit_accounting, M=2) - revision 2 (after the source-layer audit, see [13])

[0] Draw and scope snapshot. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}; --tasks 2 printed task 1 = {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 5, 5]}. Task 0 is designed exactly to that: a root problem plus one prerequisite problem; the cleaning correction credit takes 5 factors, the settlement payment takes 4. Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). Claimed here: deposit_ext_cleaning_correction_credit (tool post_cleaning_correction_credit_249da733) and deposit_ext_settlement_payment (tool pay_settlement_balance_cadbabf4). Reserved headroom for task 1 (3 prerequisites + root, 4/6/5/5 factors): the other disputed-line families (carpet/paint depreciation, repair labor, unreturned-fob count) and the Zero-Deposit Guarantee Plan payment of the part the guarantee does not cover, all untouched here; cleaning lines and cash-deposit settlement stay with task 0 only.

[1] Why this is a good test. The resident asks for one thing - settle what she still owes on her move-out balance today, with one payment of her own. Nothing in the ask names the core number. To pay the right amount the agent must (a) read in the settlement policy's own rule that 'A settlement payment is taken only after every cleaning line under an accepted dispute carries its dispute credit on the account.', (b) find in the dispute records that the whole-unit cleaning line (ee0b2708-1d3e-4716-a4a4-c41f04d14500) is under an accepted dispute with no credit on the ledger, (c) work out from the cleaning correction policy that its write is the one that brings that state about, (d) compute that credit from the floor plan's cleaning rate plus five record-driven rules (surfaces replaced -> which floor plan's rate is used, animals -> spot rate, tenancy + returned payments -> courtesy on the whole-unit charge, occupants vs bedrooms -> heavy-use charge, notice on the completed last term -> notice discount), post it, and only then (e) compute the settlement payment from the corrected ledger with four more rules (late-fee record + autopay, utility account state, days before due, dispute history of the statement) and hand the payment to the resident. One write per problem; difficulty comes from reading, reconciliation (two history windows with near-miss rows) and arithmetic.

[2] Problem-tree card. Root: deposit_ext_settlement_payment (user-owned write, on_request). Prerequisite: deposit_ext_cleaning_correction_credit (agent write, state_due). Edge settlement -> cleaning credit: kind value_input, gate = binding 'credited', form state. Prerequisite sentence (settlement rule, verbatim): 'A settlement payment is taken only after every cleaning line under an accepted dispute carries its dispute credit on the account.' Four-point test: 'only after' connective, affirmative (rewrites exactly to 'is not taken until every cleaning line ... carries its dispute credit'); a record-visible state (accepted dispute on a cleaning line + a dispute credit sourced on it); no code token; scope = the edge condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty sources a dispute credit on a cleaning line (the cleaning correction policy). Why false at the opening: deposit_disputes.cf3155a0-677d-41f9-af3c-e8b6d905adb1.dispute_status = accepted on ee0b2708-1d3e-4716-a4a4-c41f04d14500; no deposit_balance_credit row. Order: credit (step 10) then payment (step 14). Deletion sensitivity: skipping the credit gives 517.54 instead of 453.04. The persona names no prerequisite; the tools validate nothing.

[3] Base-invariant card. Credit subject deposit_balance_credit: deposit_disputes_and_amendment and deposit_balance_and_collections, both policy_scope (their gates govern reversal, reopen and referral only). Payment subject deposit_balance_payment: deposit_balance_and_collections, policy_scope. No time gate applies (temporal_feasibility []). The dispute was accepted in its window and the account reopened before the call (official rows). Declared overrides of the cleaning policy: 'withdraws the line in full' (a cleaning line accepted for a misapplied charge is corrected by one dispute credit instead), 'stains beyond normal cleaning add carpet_spot_cleaning_per_room per room' (animal-dependent spot rate) and 'at cleaning_charge_by_floor_plan for the lease's floor plan' (the combined corrected-cleaning sentence: the whole-unit charge reckoned on the surfaces left in place, the courtesy on that same charge, the heavy-use charge and the notice discount). The floor plan's cleaning rate itself is the base schedule, carried in the baseline paragraph as a plain read (rate_studio ... rate_penthouse = cleaning_charge_by_floor_plan value for value). The settlement policy overrides nothing; the remainder its allowance leaves (at most small_balance_write_off) is written off by base once due.

[4] Business-object card. Target account 97d346ae-d4c8-4ce9-bcc5-bcd0597beac5 (Standard Deposit Plan, GA, lease c7ae1310-bc54-467a-8fd2-a3b4a32389c0). Credit object: the whole-unit cleaning line ee0b2708-1d3e-4716-a4a4-c41f04d14500 (295.00), the line the accepted dispute names; the cleaning aggregate also takes the two spot-cleaning lines fd0f2799-e9d1-4684-a657-f958df1fb430 (bedroom_1) and bc1308a1-a1ce-4e57-aa1d-72d7dd3d8f2c (bedroom_3), because the corrected cleaning charge covers the whole-unit cleaning and every spot-cleaned room. Excluded from the cleaning aggregate: carpet, paint, blinds, repair and fob lines (other categories; they only feed the surfaces multiplier by their presence). Settlement object: the balance owed of the same account - billed line b2bef1a6-ae4f-4f06-bf1c-e78cc9d722d8 842.54, payment dcde8df3-409a-45c7-9e05-d52bc72cd035 300.00, and the credit written at step 9. The 800.00 application 0faa4b53-bc25-4f37-bff0-1787355d3b20 and the fundings are read but settle nothing further.

[5] Factor card - cleaning correction credit (expected 64.50; whole baseline 60.00 = the base itemization reading 235.00 + 2 x 45.00 = 325.00).
 surfaces_left_in_place (method, multi-source over two line kinds): the account carries a carpet replacement line and a paint line -> the home is cleaned as the next smaller floor plan, the whole-unit charge is the Two-Bedroom rate 195.00 instead of the Three-Bedroom 235.00 (tier two would average the two rates; tier three keeps the plan's own rate); baseline (own rate) -> 28.50.
 spot_cleaning_rate_by_animal (parameter, cross-difficulty pet): Medium Dog Addendum 'Biscuit' -> spot_rate_dog 60.00; baseline 45.00 -> 94.50.
 tenancy_cleaning_courtesy (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty lease): 57 full months and exactly one returned payment fewer than 12 full months before 2026-09-04 (2025-11-06; the 2024-10-03 return is 23 months old - the near-miss) -> courtesy_mid 0.10, taken on the whole-unit charge as reckoned on the surfaces (195.00 -> 19.50); baseline none -> 45.00.
 heavy_use_cleaning_charge (parameter, cross-difficulty lease): 5 occupants vs 3 bedrooms -> 40.00; baseline 0 -> 104.50.
 notice_cleaning_discount (parameter, cross-difficulty term): notice received 2026-05-18 on the completed last term, 74 days before the 2026-07-31 move-out -> 15.00; baseline 0 -> 49.50.
 Arithmetic: 195.00 - 19.50 + 2 x 60.00 + 40.00 - 15.00 = 320.50; 385.00 - 320.50 = 64.50.
Factor card - settlement payment (expected 453.04; whole baseline 473.26).
 late_fee_record_rate (parameter, multi-source, lease): only the 2025-02-05 late fee is fewer than 24 full months old (2024-08-05 is exactly 24 - the near-miss); autopay enrolled -> 0.02; baseline 0.01 -> 461.19.
 squared_utility_step (parameter, utility): closed with 0.00 -> 0.01; baseline 0 -> 461.19.
 early_payment_ceiling (parameter, date): 16 days before the 2026-09-20 due date -> 25.00; baseline 10.00 -> 468.04.
 dispute_history_base (method): accepted dispute, statement 21 days after move-out (> 20) -> the balance as first billed, 842.54; baseline standing 478.04 -> 463.70.
 Arithmetic: standing 842.54 - 300.00 - 64.50 = 478.04; allowance min(25.00, RND(842.54 x 0.03) = 25.28) = 25.00; payment 453.04. The 25.00 left is written off by base once due.

[6] Rule <-> compute two-way sweep. Every reading/choosing binding quotes a verbatim rule sentence (check_extended). Reverse: floor-plan schedule sentence -> plan_rate; next-smaller-plan clause -> smaller_plan_rate; surfaces sentence -> carpet_lines, paint_lines, whole_unit_charge (three different formulas); animal ladder -> has_dog, has_cat, spot_rate; courtesy ladder ('a share of the whole-unit cleaning charge as reckoned on the surfaces left in place') -> tenure_months, returns_12m, cleaning_courtesy, and the closing sentence ('less the cleaning courtesy taken on that same whole-unit cleaning charge') -> the term whole_unit_charge x cleaning_courtesy in corrected_cleaning; heavy-use ladder -> occupants, bedrooms, heavy_use_charge; notice ladder (calendar days, completed last term) -> cleaning_notice_on, cleaning_notice_days, notice_cleaning_discount; single final rounding -> corrected_cleaning; credit sentence -> result. Settlement unchanged from revision 1 (standing, 24-month late-fee window, step, ceiling on calendar days before due, base by dispute history, allowance rounded then capped, payment).

[7] initial_state. As in revision 1 plus lease_terms: five terms (new lease 2021-10-01 to 2022-07-31; renewals to 2023-07-31, 2024-07-31, 2025-07-31 superseded; the renewal 2025-08-01 to 2026-07-31 completed, notice 2026-05-18, intended move-out 2026-07-31). The 2025-11 autopay, its return and the make-good were aligned to that term's rent (2480.00; make-good 2510.00 with the 30.00 GA-capped fee). Every row is read by a gold lookup (replay closure 36/36). Nothing seeded ignites an obligation outside the tree; the balance is not yet due. Cache note: deposit_accounts.balance_owed is the opening view; tools write ledger lines and computations read the ledger.

[8] Persona. As in revision 1, with the opening ask reworded to 'you want to settle what is still owed on your move-out balance today, well before the due date, with one payment of your own' (audit O-13), so the ask selects the settlement payment rather than a plain payoff of the full standing balance. Dispute detail only on request; passive hand-over; debit card; ends at the confirmation.

[9] Reachability walk (frozen 2026-09-04 14:20 EDT): find_customers -> verify(phone, ssn) -> deposit account -> ledger -> disputes -> lease -> lease payments -> pet addenda -> lease terms -> unlock + credit (64.50) -> lease charges -> utility -> unlock_user + resident pays 453.04 by debit card. No real-world wait.

[10] Uniqueness. deposit_account_id (one account); source_transaction_id = the accepted dispute's line; payment_method debit_card (persona). Computed 64.50 and 453.04; one credit row, one payment row. The acting base of the courtesy is now fixed in prose (audit F-1): only 195.00 - 0.10 x 195.00 reads the rule.

[11] Verification (revision 2, per-task gates for task 0): EXTENDED OK; REPLAY OK (15 actions, closure 36/36); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK; GROUNDING OK; and the full difficulty block after both tasks (see the task-1 dossier [11]). Sensitivity figures from the scratch evaluator match check_compute: cleaning 28.50 / 94.50 / 45.00 / 104.50 / 49.50, all-baseline 60.00; settlement 461.19 / 461.19 / 468.04 / 463.70, all-baseline 473.26; settlement without the credit 517.54.

[12] Draft recalculation from the visible context: settlement sentence -> accepted cleaning dispute without credit -> cleaning policy; its prose yields whole-unit charge 195.00 (both surfaces replaced), courtesy 19.50 on that charge, 2 x 60.00, 40.00, -15.00 -> 320.50 -> credit 64.50; settlement prose -> 478.04 - 25.00 = 453.04. Same as gold; no second reading found.

[13] Revisions. Round 1: (a) settlement keys renamed settle_* to avoid a prose collision; (b) module-level helper removed from task_tools.py.
Round 2 (source-layer audit, audits/policy_task/move_out_deposit_accounting/0.md and _difficulty.md):
 F-1 (acting base of the cleaning courtesy) - symptom: two readings (55.80/461.74 vs 60.50/457.04); root cause: 'a share of the whole-unit cleaning rate' vs 'multiplied ..., then reduced by the courtesy'; change: the courtesy is now 'a share of the whole-unit cleaning charge as reckoned on the surfaces left in place', the closing sentence says 'less the cleaning courtesy taken on that same whole-unit cleaning charge', and compute writes whole_unit_charge - whole_unit_charge x cleaning_courtesy; result: one reading, credit 64.50, payment 453.04.
 F-2 (surfaces_left_in_place mislabelled method) - change: the factor now selects how the whole-unit charge is computed: next smaller floor plan's rate (both surfaces replaced), the average of the two plans' rates (one replaced), the plan's own rate (neither).
 F-4 (straw-man baseline of whole_unit_rate_by_floor_plan) - change: that factor is removed; the floor plan's cleaning rate (the base schedule) is a plain read stated in the baseline paragraph, so the whole baseline is now the base itemization reading (credit 60.00). The factor count stays at the drawn 5 with a new notice_cleaning_discount factor (term: notice on the completed last term), seeded with the lease's term chain and read at step 8.
 Observations: O-3 (corrected statement with no tool) - accepted, the statement re-issue is a back-office act outside this difficulty's tools; O-4 (asymmetric gating) - no task world combines a cash account with a carpet/repair/fob dispute or a guarantee account with a cleaning dispute, recorded as a known limit; O-5 ('last term' = status completed) - the cleaning, repair and guarantee-gap rules now all say 'the lease's completed last term', matching the status='completed' read; O-7 - credit docstrings no longer use 'after'; O-8 - both payment rules now say the resident pays 'themself, through the resident portal'; O-9, O-10, O-11, O-12, O-14 - accepted as observations (time-bounded base writes; group application; grounds outside the base dash list are recorded acceptances; the premium's own coverage definition is not the scored quantity; the persona's dispute ground is given only on request and carries no value); O-13 - persona ask reworded (see [8]).
Round 3 (audit revision_2: task 0 PASS on all four relationships; charter items and a coordinator request):
 Rename (coordinator, cross-difficulty merge): the customer's full name is now Marisela Thornquist and her email marisela.thornquist43@outlook.com (local part still ending in 43); phone 404-554-7163, SSN last four 4729, date of birth and every id are unchanged. The rename is carried through initial_state, user_scenario, db_closure and this dossier; the gold verifies with phone + SSN, so no argument changed.
 O-18 - the cleaning rule now states the floor-plan order (Studio Residence, One-Bedroom Residence, One-Bedroom Den Residence, Two-Bedroom Residence, Three-Bedroom Residence, Penthouse Residence, smallest to largest) that 'next smaller floor plan' follows; Three-Bedroom -> Two-Bedroom 195.00 here, figures unchanged (credit 64.50, payment 453.04). O-19 concerns the carpet rule of task 1 and was reworded there; no task-0 figure moves.
user_scenario: You are Marisela Thornquist, 38, a pharmacist who lived for almost five years in apartment 4-508 at Larkspur Midtown Atlanta with your husband and your three kids and your dog, Biscuit, until you moved out on July 31. You are calling from your car on a lunch break, organised and a little brisk, because you want the last piece of the move behind you. Open by saying you are a former resident and you want to settle what is still owed on your move-out balance today, well before the due date, with one payment of your own. You give your mobile number, 404-554-7163, right away so they can find you. When they ask you to confirm who you are, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 4729; only if they need one more detail do you add your email, marisela.thornquist43@outlook.com. You remember the final statement came in late August and showed a balance of a little over eight hundred forty dollars, and that you already paid 300 dollars toward it on September 2 with your debit card; you do not remember the exact figures beyond that and you expect the agent to look them up. Only if the agent asks whether you disputed anything on the statement do you say yes: the whole-home cleaning charge looked like a penthouse price for a three-bedroom, you filed a dispute on it in the portal, and you later got an email saying the dispute was accepted. You do not know what that changes and you leave the arithmetic to them. If the agent explains that something has to be recorded on their side before your payment can be taken, you tell them to go ahead and you wait. When the agent gives you the amount to pay and hands you the payment step, you will pay with your debit card, in exactly the amount and on the account they tell you, and you read back the confirmation number the portal shows you. If the agent asks how you want to pay, you say debit card. You never ask for anything beyond settling this balance. Once your payment has gone through and you have the confirmation, you thank them and end the call.

Its only gate governs collections referral; a credit that reduces the balance owed is within its scope once a balance owed stands, as the 842.54 balance owed line shows.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's resident profile from the mobile number she states, returning her customer reference number and the credentials on file.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later lookup and write is keyed to this customer reference number; without it neither the deposit account nor the lease can be found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller with two stated credentials (mobile number and last four of the SSN) against the profile and record the outcome.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be verified in-session before any account detail is discussed or any write is made; two matching credentials meet the tool's threshold.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the security deposit account: program (Standard Deposit Plan), status move_out_review (reopened), move-out date 2026-07-31, statement date 2026-08-21 and balance owed due date 2026-09-20.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The settlement ceiling reads the days from the handling date to the due date, the settlement base reads the move-out and statement dates, and every write needs the deposit account reference number.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every deposit ledger line: the three cleaning lines (whole-unit 295.00, bedroom_1 45.00, bedroom_3 45.00), the carpet replacement and paint lines, the 800.00 application, the 842.54 balance owed and the 300.00 payment of 2026-09-02.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The cleaning charged, the spot-cleaned rooms and the surfaces multiplier of the cleaning correction, and the billed, paid and credited totals of the settlement all rest on these rows; the disputed whole-unit line's reference number is the source of the credit.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the disputes on the statement: one dispute against the whole-unit cleaning line, status accepted, and no other.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The accepted cleaning dispute is what makes the cleaning correction credit due and is the state the settlement payment's prerequisite sentence waits on (a cleaning line under an accepted dispute without its dispute credit); it also puts the settlement base on its dispute-history tier.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the lease payment history, including the two returned payments (2024-10-03 and 2025-11-06).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The cleaning courtesy tier counts returned payments dated fewer than twelve full months before the handling date: only the 2025-11-06 return counts, the 2024-10-03 return is outside the window.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the animals registered on the lease: one Medium Dog Addendum (a dog, Biscuit), ended at move-out.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.deposit_account_id: 97d346ae-d4c8-4ce9-bcc5-bcd0597beac5 — basis: the deposit account lookup returns exactly one account for this resident, and the tool's Args say the account reference number is read from that lookup; uniqueness: the resident holds one lease and one deposit account (deposit_agg_multi_holding), so no other value is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_transaction_id: ee0b2708-1d3e-4716-a4a4-c41f04d14500 — basis: the policy rule says the credit is 'posted against the disputed cleaning line', and the dispute lookup returns one accepted dispute whose line is ee0b2708-1d3e-4716-a4a4-c41f04d14500, the whole-unit cleaning line of 295.00; uniqueness: the two spot-cleaning lines carry no dispute, and no other line of the account is under an accepted dispute.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 64.50 = cleaning charged 385.00 (295.00 + 45.00 + 45.00) less the corrected cleaning charge 320.50. The whole-unit cleaning charge is reckoned on the surfaces left in place: the account carries both a carpet replacement line and a paint line, so the home is cleaned as the next smaller floor plan and the charge is the Two-Bedroom rate 195.00 (not the Three-Bedroom rate 235.00). Cleaning courtesy 0.10 taken on that same 195.00 (tenancy 57 full months from 2021-10-01 to 2026-07-31, exactly one returned payment dated fewer than twelve full months before 2026-09-04 - the 2025-11-06 return; the 2024-10-03 return is outside) = 19.50, so 175.50; plus 2 spot-cleaned rooms x 60.00 (a dog was registered on the lease) = 120.00; plus the heavy-use charge 40.00 (5 approved occupants exceed the 3 bedrooms by two or more); less the notice cleaning discount 15.00 (notice on the completed last term received 2026-05-18, 74 days before move-out, at least 60). 175.50 + 120.00 + 40.00 - 15.00 = 320.50; 385.00 - 320.50 = 64.50.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: The settlement payment policy (deposit_ext_settlement_payment) uniquely computes 453.04 on the world after the cleaning credit; the payment is the resident's own act, so she runs the tool herself.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.deposit_account_id: 97d346ae-d4c8-4ce9-bcc5-bcd0597beac5 — basis: the agent reads the deposit account reference number from the deposit account lookup and gives it to the resident with the amount; uniqueness: the resident holds one deposit account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 453.04 = balance owed standing 478.04 (billed 842.54 - paid 300.00 - credited 64.50) less the settlement allowance 25.00; allowance = settlement rate 0.02 (exactly one late fee posted in the twenty-four full months before 2026-09-04, the 2025-02-05 fee, with autopay enrolled; the 2024-08-05 fee is 24 full months old and outside) plus the step 0.01 (utility account closed with a zero balance) = 0.03, applied to the settlement base 842.54 (a dispute was accepted and the statement of 2026-08-21 was issued 21 days after the 2026-07-31 move-out, more than disposition_statement_days 20, so the base is the balance owed as first billed) = 25.28, held to the ceiling 25.00 (the payment is made 16 calendar days before the 2026-09-20 due date, at least early_days 14, so the ceiling is small_balance_write_off 25.00); 478.04 - 25.00 = 453.04.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_method: debit_card — basis: the customer line 'you will pay with your debit card' in the scenario and the tool's Args: 'debit_card — a debit card the resident enters in the portal'; uniqueness: the resident states only a debit card; ach_one_time and credit_card are not what she chooses, money_order and cashiers_check are handed in at the leasing office, not paid on the call, and ach_direct_deposit, paper_check and not_applicable are never paying instruments.

edges.condition: For every deposit dispute with status accepted that is recorded against a cleaning line of the account, the account's transactions include a dispute credit whose source line is that cleaning line.
edges.policy_source: A settlement payment is taken only after every cleaning line under an accepted dispute carries its dispute credit on the account.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only dispute on the statement is recorded against the whole-unit cleaning line and has status accepted, but no dispute credit stands on the account for that line: the account's transactions hold funding, itemized lines, the 800.00 application, the 842.54 balance owed and one 300.00 payment, and no deposit_balance_credit row at all.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The call at step 10 creates a deposit_transactions row with event_type deposit_balance_credit, line_category dispute_credit, source_transaction_id ee0b2708-1d3e-4716-a4a4-c41f04d14500 and amount 64.50; the accepted cleaning dispute then carries its dispute credit, and the settlement payment's credited binding reads 64.50 instead of 0.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single edge (settlement payment <- cleaning correction credit); there is no parallel prerequisite to reorder. The order itself is pinned by the prerequisite sentence 'A settlement payment is taken only after every cleaning line under an accepted dispute carries its dispute credit on the account.', and it is observable: paying first computes 517.54 (credited 0.00) instead of 453.04 and then leaves the credit to over-reduce the balance, a different terminal state from gold.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the step-10 credit and replaying the rest: the settlement payment recomputes to 517.54 instead of 453.04 (credited 0.00, standing 542.54 instead of 478.04; the settlement base stays 842.54 because the statement was late, the allowance stays 25.00), and the terminal ledger lacks the 64.50 dispute-credit row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The scenario asks only to settle what is still owed on the move-out balance with one payment of her own. It never mentions a credit, a correction or anything that must be done first; the cleaning dispute is disclosed only if the agent asks whether anything was disputed, and even then only as the resident's own act and the acceptance email she received, with 'You do not know what that changes and you leave the arithmetic to them.' Her only prerequisite-related line is passive: 'If the agent explains that something has to be recorded on their side before your payment can be taken, you tell them to go ahead and you wait.'
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: pay_settlement_balance_cadbabf4 in task_tools.py reads the account only to copy its customer_id and then calls ctx.create('deposit_transactions', ...) with the amount and instrument passed; it checks no dispute, no credit and no balance, raises nothing and returns 'Payment received ...' whether or not the cleaning credit exists. post_cleaning_correction_credit_249da733 likewise writes the credit line unconditionally.
